subject.title: Session files should never be deleted — rename .deleted.* to .archived.*

question: Should retained session transcript archives become permanent-by-default history artifacts, or should OpenClaw keep retention and disk-budget deletion with clearer archive naming and explicit operator controls?
rationale: Current code intentionally supports both retained archive files and physical cleanup, while this issue asks to change the product storage contract for user conversation history; automation cannot safely choose that policy or its migration surface.

options.title: Preserve By Default
options.body: Rename or move retained transcript archives, stop default retention/disk-budget purge of those archives, and add explicit documented cleanup controls for operators who choose physical deletion.

options.title: Clarify Retention Contract
options.body: Keep cleanup behavior but rename/docs/config split the states so operators can distinguish retained archives from physically deleted transcripts.

options.title: Keep Current Policy
options.body: Leave `.deleted.*` and current cleanup semantics in place, accepting the reported confusion and data-loss risk as outside the core contract.

recommendation.title: Preserve By Default
recommendation.body: Rename or move retained transcript archives, stop default retention/disk-budget purge of those archives, and add explicit documented cleanup controls for operators who choose physical deletion.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the current blame carrier and recent PR author for the central archive/disk-budget code paths, making them the best available routing owner from inspected history.
